name: Hammond Creation Laboratory
function: Genome assembly, viability screening, embryo development, incubation
description: Every asset in this archive originates here or from its Sorna equivalent. The laboratory survived the 1993 abandonment largely intact, was refitted for the Jurassic World build, and continued producing assets under the same division head for over thirty years. Its unusual feature was placement: it sat inside the guest circulation route, and part of the process was visible from a moving walkway.
capacity: Fourteen incubation bays; sequencing and viability suites; cold storage for viable embryos
condition: Destroyed. Contents partially removed prior to the 2018 evacuation.
notes: Embryo cold storage was emptied before the island was lost. The destination of that material is not recorded in this archive.

name: Jurassic Park Visitor Centre
function: Guest reception, exhibition, park control, staff accommodation
description: The building the first park was organised around: reception and rotunda above, control room and laboratory below. Its design assumed a staffed control room at all times, and the 1993 failure demonstrated what happened when that assumption did not hold. Left to the forest for twenty-two years, it was partially reclaimed and briefly re-entered during the 2015 incident.
capacity: Rotunda, two exhibition wings, control room, sub-level laboratory access
condition: Destroyed in the 2018 volcanic event after twenty-five years derelict.
notes: The control room retained partial power in 2015 via the original auxiliary circuit — the only 1993 system still functioning at that date.

name: Tyrannosaur Paddock
function: Containment and exhibition of the primary tyrannosaur asset
description: A single-occupant enclosure on the main tour road, bounded by a 3.5 m electrified barrier and a concrete drop on the guest side. The barrier was the only thing containing the asset, and it was on the same circuit as everything else on the island. When that circuit went down in June 1993, the enclosure ceased to exist as a containment structure.
capacity: One adult tyrannosaur
condition: Derelict from 1993; destroyed 2018.
notes: Post-incident review recommended independent circuits for every predator enclosure. The recommendation was implemented in the Jurassic World build.

name: Velociraptor Research Paddock
function: Containment, behavioural conditioning and imprint research on the Velociraptor pack
description: Built around a working hypothesis rather than an exhibit: that a Velociraptor pack would accept a human as pack structure if imprinted from hatching. The programme worked, within limits its own staff described precisely — the animals were not tame, the relationship was not control, and it held only while the pack hierarchy held. Corporate interest in weaponising that result was the reason the programme was eventually overruled.
capacity: Four-animal pack; overhead observation gantry; feed cage and handling race
condition: Destroyed 2015 during the containment failure; site later lost with the island.
notes: Field research from this facility is the most complete behavioural dataset InGen holds on any predator asset.

name: Paddock 11
function: Containment of the Indominus rex programme asset prior to exhibition
description: Twelve metres of reinforced concrete, built in Sector 5 away from guest sightlines, and defeated by its occupant within three years. The enclosure was specified against a threat profile written by the division that created the asset. It did not account for thermal concealment, and it did not account for an animal that would injure itself to test a barrier.
capacity: One asset; observation gallery; crane-fed delivery system
condition: Breached 2015, destroyed 2018.
notes: The breach was initially assessed as an escape over the wall. Review established the asset had never left the enclosure and was inducing a door-opening response.

name: Main Street Resort Complex
function: Guest accommodation, retail, dining, transport interchange, park control
description: The commercial heart of the second build and the reason it was solvent. Hotels, retail, the monorail interchange and the innovation centre sat inside a single pedestrian core holding twenty thousand people at peak. Its containment assumption was distance: nothing dangerous was ever supposed to reach it. In 2015 several things did, simultaneously.
capacity: Approximately 20,000 guests at peak occupancy
condition: Evacuated 2015; destroyed 2018.
notes: The 2015 evacuation moved the full guest population off-island without a single guest fatality attributable to the evacuation itself.

name: Lagoon Exhibition Stadium
function: Public feeding exhibition; marine asset husbandry and containment
description: Tiered seating on a retractable platform above an engineered saltwater basin, built so an audience could watch a marine predator feed from directly overhead. The husbandry was competent and the exhibition was the park's most attended attraction. The containment was always conditional on a barrier at the ocean channel.
capacity: Retractable spectator platform; one marine asset; filtered ocean exchange channel
condition: Destroyed 2018. Ocean channel barrier failed during the event.
notes: Asset departed via the channel during the evacuation and has not been recovered.

name: Site B Operations Compound
function: Production administration, asset processing, transfer staging, power generation
description: The industrial half of InGen that investors never saw. Processing sheds, a fuel depot, a gas-powered generator hall and the loading infrastructure to move sedated juveniles to the Nublar transport. Everything about it was built for throughput, and everything about it was abandoned in under seventy-two hours when Hurricane Clarissa arrived.
capacity: Processing sheds, generator hall, fuel store, transfer yard
condition: Abandoned 1995 and never re-secured. Structural condition unknown since 2001.
notes: Assets in process at the time of evacuation were released rather than destroyed. That decision produced the Sorna population.

name: Site B Hatchery
function: Incubation, hatching, neonatal care, imprint management, viability culling
description: Where the assets were actually born. Climate-controlled incubation rows, neonatal pens and the records room that tracked every clutch against its genome batch. The imprint protocols developed here — deciding what a hatchling saw first — later underpinned the Nublar behavioural programme.
capacity: Multiple incubation rows; neonatal pens; batch records room
condition: Abandoned 1995. Interior condition unknown.
notes: Hatchery batch records were not recovered. Any reconstruction of early lineage depends on Nublar duplicates.

name: Site B Worker Village
function: Accommodation, mess, medical station, communications for production staff
description: Housing for the people who ran the production site — a mess hall, a medical station, a radio room and enough accommodation for a working population that corporate records describe only as contractors. It was evacuated in the same seventy-two hours as the rest of the island, and personal effects were left behind.
capacity: Accommodation blocks, mess, medical station, radio room
condition: Abandoned and substantially overgrown. Occupied by nesting assets as of 2001.
notes: The village is inside the interior basin territory and should be treated as an active nesting site, not a structure.

name: Lockwood Sub-Level Laboratory
type: Concealed genetic research and holding facility
function: Originally private genetics research; latterly unauthorised asset holding and auction staging
description: Three levels beneath a private house, and chronologically the first InGen laboratory of any kind. The original work here established that de-extinction was viable at all. In 2018 the same rooms were used to cage assets shipped off Isla Nublar and to stage their sale to private buyers, using a laboratory that no regulator knew existed.
capacity: Laboratory suites, holding cages, auction floor, vehicle access tunnel
condition: Compromised. Holding cages breached during the 2018 incident; assets released to open ground.
notes: The genetic work carried out here in 2018 was not authorised by InGen and is not reflected in any programme record.

name: Biosyn Research Complex
function: Genetic research, agricultural pathogen work, asset observation, hyperloop transit
description: A competitor's research campus built into the rim of a containment valley, with laboratories, accommodation, a control hub and a transit link running beneath the basin floor. Its stated purpose is sanctuary science. Its recovered output includes an engineered agricultural pathogen with no sanctuary application whatever.
capacity: Laboratory levels, accommodation, control hub, sub-basin transit terminus
condition: Operational. Amber storage and part of the laboratory level were lost to fire in 2022.
notes: Competitor facility. Assessed from recovered material and testimony, not inspection.

name: Biosyn Amber Extraction Works
function: Extraction and processing of amber-preserved biological material
description: The reason the valley was selected. The Dolomite deposit is unusually rich in insect-bearing amber, giving its operator a renewable supply of source material rather than dependence on a fixed sample library. Whoever controls a productive amber seam controls the front of the entire de-extinction pipeline.
capacity: Extraction galleries, sorting and processing floor, secure sample vault
condition: Operational. Sample vault damaged during the 2022 fire.
notes: Strategic significance is high. InGen has no comparable renewable source.

name: Saint-Hubert Research Station
function: Genetic research outside exhibition-viable parameters
description: A laboratory built where nobody would ask to see the animals. Work here proceeded without any requirement that an asset be presentable, transportable or survivable in a guest environment, which removed the single largest constraint on the genetics division. Several specimens produced here were never assigned exhibition classifications because none applied.
capacity: Sequencing and assembly suites, containment cells, incubation, staff quarters
condition: Sealed following the 2010 incident. Interior state unknown.
notes: Facility was sealed with assets alive on site. No entry has been authorised since.

name: Corporate Records Vault
function: Custody of the complete asset, personnel and operational record
description: The physical archive this index is drawn from. Holds the original creation logs, containment specifications and incident files for every InGen programme, including material never entered into any digital system. Access is logged individually and retained indefinitely.
capacity: Climate-controlled stacks, cold storage annexe, reading room
condition: Operational. Holdings intact; several 1993-era files remain sealed.
notes: The only facility on record whose function is the record itself. Its 1993 sealing order has never been lifted or explained.

name: Palo Alto Genetics Division
function: Genome sequencing, gap-sequence research and programme oversight
description: Where the reconstruction method was developed before any island existed. The amber extraction technique, the amphibian gap-sequence protocol and every viability threshold still quoted in asset files were established in these laboratories, and the results were sent to Site B to be grown.
capacity: Sequencing suites, amber preparation, cold storage, computation floor
condition: Operational. Research scope narrowed substantially after 1997.
notes: The amphibian sequence chosen here to close genome gaps is the direct cause of the unplanned breeding observed on Isla Nublar.

name: Mantah Corp Bio-Engineering Compound
type: Concealed genetic engineering and behavioural conditioning site
function: Behavioural conditioning and control-implant research on live assets
description: A privately built compound operating outside every regulatory framework that governs InGen sites. Work here centred on controlling asset behaviour directly through implanted hardware rather than through containment, across biomes engineered to hold incompatible species on one island.
capacity: Conditioning arenas, implant laboratory, control centre, artificial biome plant
condition: Compromised. Programme exposed and control systems disabled.
notes: The archive holds this record because the assets involved originate from InGen genetic material. The programme itself was never InGen's.

name: Lagoon Containment Grid
type: Submerged barrier and water management system
function: Retention of the marine asset within the engineered lagoon
description: The engineering beneath the exhibition stadium: a submerged gate system, depth-graded barrier nets and the pumps that held the lagoon at working level. Designed for an animal substantially smaller than the one it ended up containing, and never revised upward.
capacity: Sea gate, three barrier tiers, pump house, feeding rig
condition: Compromised. Sea gate left open during the 2015 evacuation and never closed.
notes: The gate remained open through the 2018 eruption. The marine asset's departure to open ocean required no breach of any kind.

name: Site B Interior Field Station
type: Field observation and sample collection station
function: Population observation and sample collection in the uncontrolled interior
description: A light prefabricated post pushed into the interior basin to monitor animals released from the hatchery. Abandoned during the Hurricane Clarissa evacuation with equipment and logbooks in place, which is why it remains the best surviving record of Site B population behaviour before the island was left to itself.
capacity: Two observation huts, sample store, radio mast
condition: Abandoned. Structures standing but overgrown; interior reclaimed.
notes: The station logs end mid-entry. Nothing in them anticipates that the populations would sustain themselves without intervention.

name: Northern Sector Perimeter Station
type: Perimeter monitoring and access control station
function: Access control and monitoring for the closed northern sector
description: The only staffed position in the sector kept off the park map. Controlled road access to the restricted paddocks north of the resort and logged every vehicle through it, which is how the archive can establish who visited Paddock 11 and when.
capacity: Gatehouse, monitoring room, vehicle inspection bay
condition: Decommissioned. Overrun during the 2015 containment failure; not reoccupied.
notes: Access logs recovered from this station contradict the official account of how frequently the Indominus enclosure was entered.
